name: Ravi Kumar
history: On 2026-03-10, Ravi Kumar of Ravi Traders was sent a formal email reminder for invoice INV-1620 (Rs 32,000). He did not reply.
On 2026-03-14, a short WhatsApp message to Ravi Kumar got a reply within 10 minutes; he promised to pay by Friday 2026-03-20.
On 2026-03-20, Ravi Kumar broke his promise and did not pay INV-1620. He paid 9 days later, on 2026-03-29, after a second WhatsApp nudge.
On 2026-06-02, Ravi Kumar promised to pay INV-1788 (Rs 41,000) by the 12th, then paid on the 25th. He tends to promise specific dates and slip by one to two weeks.
Ravi Kumar responds to short, friendly WhatsApp messages and ignores long formal emails. Pressure or threats make him go silent.
On 2026-08-01, offering Ravi Kumar a two-part payment split for INV-1901 worked: he paid half immediately and half within a week.

name: Meera Nair
history: Meera Nair of Meera Interiors has paid every invoice so far, typically 2 to 4 days after a polite email reminder.
On 2026-05-05, a phone call to Meera Nair annoyed her; she said she prefers everything in writing by email.
Meera Nair pays via bank transfer and usually sends a screenshot confirmation the same day.
On 2026-07-18, Meera Nair was 6 days late on INV-1850 because her accountant was on leave; she apologised and paid the same afternoon after a gentle email.
Meera Nair values courtesy and is a high-value long-term client, so avoid firm or pushy language.

name: Kiran Reddy
history: Kiran Reddy of Kiran Electronics has ignored 3 email reminders and 2 WhatsApp messages across the last two invoices.
On 2026-04-11, a phone call to Kiran Reddy before 11 AM worked: he paid INV-1544 (Rs 74,000) the same day.
On 2026-06-20, Kiran Reddy did not answer messages for 3 weeks, then paid within hours of a morning phone call.
Kiran Reddy is usually unavailable in the afternoon; calls between 9 and 11 AM reach him.
Kiran Reddy has never formally disputed an invoice; the delays look like inattention, not unwillingness.

name: Anita Sharma
history: On 2026-07-05, Anita Sharma of Sunrise Logistics disputed INV-1877, saying 3 of the delivered units arrived damaged.
On 2026-07-12, a credit note of Rs 6,500 was issued to Anita Sharma; she paid the remaining amount within 2 days.
Anita Sharma pays quickly once a dispute is resolved in writing, and dislikes being reminded while a dispute is open.
On 2026-08-20, Anita Sharma said INV-2070 is on hold until proof of delivery is shared; the proof of delivery has not been sent yet.
Anita Sharma responds best to emails that include documents (delivery proof, credit notes) and a clear next step.
